_comment: Regression example proving the Monday-sale / Friday-refund scenario: the refund references Monday's Sale unchanged, but is attributed to Friday's own processing FiscalDay/Shift — never inserted into Monday's (closed) FiscalDay. Demonstrates Stage 2 invariants #67-70.

original_sale_monday._note: fd-2026-09-14-terminal-1 is now CLOSED (Monday's Z-Reading was generated at end of day).

refund_response_201._context_note: terminal_id happens to be the same physical terminal, but fiscal_day_id and shift_id are FRIDAY's own OPEN fiscal day/shift (fd-2026-09-18-...), completely distinct from Monday's fd-2026-09-14-terminal-1, which remains CLOSED and untouched.

items._calc: owed_after_this_event = round(100.00 * 1/2, 2) = 50.00; minus SUM(prior refund_item amounts for si-monday-1) = 0.00 -> this event = 50.00 (Stage 2 cumulative-recompute-then-subtract rule).

refund_response_201._settlement_reconciliation: SUM(settlements.amount) = 50.00 = refund.refund_total exactly (Stage 2 invariant #70). CASH settlement reduces shift-friday-1-b's expected drawer cash (invariant #71); Monday's original sale, its terminal_id/fiscal_day_id/shift_id, and its SALE-type stock_movement are all completely untouched.
